deliveryProcedure: Run only after the Build review passes, one repository at a time.

Fetch origin. If origin/main moved past the recorded base, rebase the label commit onto it, revalidate the exact message with that repository's commitlint, and rerun its pinned README tests if the rebase changed README.md, a modified .csproj or a test that reads them. Parties already needs this: its origin/main is 64085d9f, not the recorded base 87a7b600.

A repository whose label commit already reached main out of band (status merged-unreviewed; currently Folders, through the concurrent /pushall merge f1f63909) skips the rebase and the push: list and record the main runs for its mergedCommit and for the later main head as in the next step, then regenerate and re-verify as below.
Push the label commit to main. If the push is rejected, record status push-rejected with the reason in the outcomes file, regenerate this register, and halt for the user.

List every main run for the pushed commit with gh run list -R Hexalith/Hexalith.<Repo> --commit <sha> and wait for each to finish. Record each run id, workflow and conclusion. If any run does not conclude success, record status ci-red, regenerate this register, and halt for the user without patching around the failure.

Regenerate this register with build-labels.py --rev <repo>=<pushed sha> --outcomes <file>. This re-records the base, the pushed commit, mergedCommit, every row's commit, the README blob and hashes, the label and Description anchors and hashes from the pushed blobs, and mainCiRuns.
Rerun verify-labels.py with --rev <repo>=<pushed sha> for every repository, against the pushed commits.
Rescan this directory into a new receipt.
labelHashDefinition: Label sha256 covers the exact UTF-8 label line as committed, without a line terminator. Description sha256 covers the committed line that holds the prefix, without a line terminator. README sha256 covers the whole committed blob after Git normalization. messageSha256 covers the commit message as git log -1 --format=%B prints it, with its trailing newlines collapsed to exactly one.
